title: UNM Health — the trauma center that turned ambulances away

scenes.narration: [serious] A cyberattack sent ambulances away from New Mexico's only top trauma center.
UNM Hospital runs the state's only Level 1 trauma center, for the worst injuries.
On October 26, staff saw messages on their screens. They claimed patient data was stolen.
Ambulances went elsewhere for about two hours. Outpatient surgeries stopped for the day.
A new gang called Byod claimed the attack. Its claims are unverified.
By the next day, UNM said key systems were back. It says core servers were never reached.
The FBI is assisting. For about two hours, New Mexico had no top trauma care.

facts.claim: UNM operates New Mexico's only Level 1 trauma center; the closure left the state without an ED able to treat the most serious injuries; ~100,000 ER visits a year
On Monday Oct 26, 2026 employees saw messages on their computers claiming student, employee and patient data had been stolen
Ambulances were diverted to health systems in Albuquerque and Santa Fe for about two hours
UNM Health suspended outpatient surgeries and appointments on Oct 26
A group called Byod claimed the attack Monday evening, saying it compromised 36,000 machines; it emerged last month; claims unverified, UNM did not confirm ransomware
UNM said all critical electronic systems were back online and clinics resumed Oct 27; the event affected some end-user devices but did not penetrate core systems or servers
FBI spokesperson Margot Cravens said the agency was 'assisting our partner'
